rationale: The paused lead is left for a later run, and its hand-off is only useful if the probe design is concrete rather than restated as an intention. Working it out is cheap and needs no execution, so the question's discriminator and resume conditions are updated with the specific construction: a single-voter cluster whose FSM sleeps inside Apply, a flood of applies to fill the mutation channel, and an independent call that must be answered by the main loop as the stall probe, with a fast-FSM and a bounded-rate control.

investigations.discriminator: Build a cluster whose FSM sleeps for a fixed interval inside Apply (shorter than the heartbeat timeout) and, using a single-voter cluster so that no election intervenes, fill the FSM mutation channel by driving applies at a rate the FSM cannot match. Probe the main loop with a call that must be answered there - VerifyLeader is the cleanest, since for a single voter verifyLeader responds inside the main loop, so a future that stays unresolved is direct evidence that the loop is blocked - and measure that call's latency against a baseline taken before the flood and against a control in which Apply is fast and the apply rate is bounded. Record the FSM lag, the channel occupancy, the probe latency and the leader's state, and note whether the stall ends when the FSM drains rather than by any internal action, which the source reading already predicts because the send has no rejection path and its only other arm is the shutdown channel.
resume_conditions: A run has enough time to build a sleeping-FSM harness, drive a flood of applies and interpret the receipt; the source half of the question is already answered and recorded, so only the behavioural half remains.
